title: Skin: The Body's Barrier
hook: Spread out, your skin would cover about two square metres — the largest organ you have, and the only one you wear on the outside.
key_points: Skin is the body's largest organ, forming a continuous barrier against the outside world.
It keeps water and nutrients in while keeping germs, chemicals, and UV out.
It helps regulate body temperature through sweating and by widening or narrowing blood vessels.
Packed with receptors, skin is also a sense organ for touch, pressure, temperature, and pain.
content_html: Your skin is the largest organ you have, and it does far more than hold you together. It is a waterproof, germ-proof barrier that seals your insides off from a world full of microbes, chemicals, and ultraviolet light, while keeping precious water and nutrients from leaking out.
extra_html: Skin is built in layers: a tough outer epidermis that constantly sheds and renews itself, a thicker dermis below it packed with blood vessels, nerve endings, sweat glands, and hair follicles, and a fatty layer beneath that cushions and insulates. Beyond protection, skin is a key player in homeostasis — when you overheat, sweat glands release moisture that cools you as it evaporates, and surface blood vessels widen to shed heat; when you are cold, they narrow to hold heat in. As NIH MedlinePlus describes, skin is also a sense organ, threaded with receptors that report touch, pressure, temperature, and pain back to the brain.

related.title: Homeostasis: Staying Balanced
related.hook: Your body works hard to keep its inside world steady — temperature, water, blood sugar — no matter what's happening outside. That balancing act is homeostasis.

related.title: The Senses
related.hook: Light, sound, chemicals, and pressure can't enter your brain directly — your senses translate all of them into the one language your neurons understand: electrical signals.

related.title: The Circulatory System
related.hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.

flashcards.prompt: Why is skin considered the largest organ of the body?
flashcards.back_html: It covers the entire body surface — roughly two square metres in an adult — and works as a single, continuous organ with several vital jobs.

flashcards.prompt: How does skin help cool you down on a hot day?

choices.text: By sweating and widening blood vessels to release heat
By absorbing heat and storing it permanently
By thickening to trap more warmth

flashcards.explanation_html: Sweat evaporates and carries heat away, and blood vessels near the surface widen to radiate heat — both help keep your core temperature steady.

flashcards.prompt: Besides being a barrier, what other major role does skin play?

choices.text: It senses touch, pressure, temperature, and pain

flashcards.explanation_html: Skin is densely packed with sensory receptors, making it a true sense organ in addition to a protective wrapper.
